method.round_aggregation: median/minimum/maximum of three independent per-process round medians; not a pooled sample median
method.timed_interval: fresh graph construction and invoke through synchronization; input creation/upload, setup, numerical checking and returned-output release are outside this interval
method.warmup: at least 10 calls and 1 second, actual iterations recorded
method.fuga_over_torch: Fuga latency / Torch eager latency; greater than one is slower

limits: End-to-end latency includes Python graph construction, submission and completion wait, not pure kernel execution.
CUDA matmul baseline uses IEEE and the main final comparison uses TF32. The general-input IEEE control provides a matched-precision comparison.
CPU remains f32 with no TF32; OpenBLAS may change contraction and reduction order relative to the previous native implementation.
Groups ran sequentially, with backend order rotated within each group. Cross-group changes are not paired simultaneous trials.
ASK resident/pool bytes and PyTorch allocated/reserved bytes have different allocator scopes. ASK counters exclude hidden driver/library allocations.
RSS is the peak for the whole worker process including framework import, inputs, compilation and libraries; it is not live tensor memory.
Graph and launch counts are ASK plan counters; a captured cuBLAS child is one logical step, not necessarily one hardware kernel.
Total counters scale with measured warmup_iterations. Compare normalized counters per execution and static graph sizes.
Numerical verification is performed by the worker reference; this analysis verifies flags, finite errors, counts and consistency against raw timing samples.
The latency matrix measures fp32 row-major inputs. Other dtype/layout contracts are covered by separate numerical tests.
Matmul inputs are structured rank-one operands with alternating signs; general inputs use non-dyadic stored values. Cancellation is covered by separate correctness tests.
GPU clocks were not locked. Duration-based warmup mitigates initial low-frequency effects; three-round ranges remain part of the evidence.
